title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-18
content:
Daily scratchpad - running quick evals + quant notes

Context / goal:
- Want to baseline instruction-following quality + latency for a few tuned variants we might ship in Redwood Optimize suggestions. Focus on small/med open models we expect customers to run in Dedicated or Private.
- Quick comparison: redwood-v2-small (float16 baseline) vs gptj-6b (f16) vs gptj-6b-4bit (quant via bitsandbytes) vs l2o-6b-4bit (llama.cpp / q4_0)

Quick plan for today:
- Run 200-sample instruction eval (subset of our instr-follow set) for each model+quant config. Collect: exact-match (where applicable), rouge/bleu-ish, and a judgement-ish quality score (0-3) from our heuristic classifier + a small human check on 20 samples.
- Measure latency p50/p95 (single-stream), and batch throughput for batch sizes 1,4,8. Also check peak GPU memory for each config.
- Note any decoding artifacts with 4-bit (repetition, truncation).

Commands / snippets used:
- bnb eval (Py): python eval/run_instruct_eval.py --model gptj-6b --dtype float16 --prompts ./prompts/instr-subset-200.json --out out/gptj-f16.json
- bnb 4-bit: python eval/run_instruct_eval.py --model gptj-6b --quant bitsandbytes --bnb-config q4_0 --prompts ... --out out/gptj-q4.json
- llama.cpp q4_0: ./bin/llama_eval -m l2o-6b-q4.bin -p ./prompts/instr-subset-200.txt -b 1 -o out/l2o-q4.txt
- measure latency: /usr/local/bin/latency_probe --model-path /models/gptj-6b --mode single --samples 200 > out/lat_gptj.txt

Preliminary results (raw observations, noisy):
- redwood-v2-small (f16): p50 ~ 75ms/token, p95 ~ 210ms/token on A10x (dedicated pool). Quality: baseline strong on instruction rephrasing / summarization tasks. Memory ~12GB.
- gptj-6b (f16): p50 ~ 95ms/token, p95 ~ 260ms/token. Quality slightly worse on multi-step reasoning; good for straightforward Q&A.
- gptj-6b q4_0 (bnb): p50 ~ 65ms/token (surprisingly lower), p95 ~ 240ms/token. BUT noticed increased repetition on longer outputs, and occasional tokenization mismatch around code fences. Memory ~7.5GB.
- l2o-6b q4 (llama.cpp): p50 ~ 140ms/token (CPU fallback on the instance), quality drops on instruct prompts that require multi-turn context retention. Memory small (2GB). Good for edge-case on-prem low-cost.

Initial quality deltas (heuristic classifier on 200 samples):
- redwood-v2-small: mean score 2.6/3, std 0.4
- gptj-f16: 2.2/3, std 0.6
- gptj-q4-bnb: 2.0/3, std 0.7 (lower on code and tables)
- l2o-q4: 1.7/3, std 0.9

Human spot-check (20 samples, quick notes):
- gptj-q4: 3/20 had hallucinated numeric facts; 4/20 had mild repetition; 2/20 had broken markdown/code fence rendering.
- redwood-v2-small: 1/20 minor omission in multi-step chain.

Actionable takeaways so far:
- bitsandbytes q4_0 gives a surprisingly good latency and memory win; quality cost is present but may be acceptable for many customers if we flag prompts with heavy code/table usage. Consider shipping a "quantized" model variant for cost-conscious Dedicated pools with an auto-fallback route to f16 for flagged prompts.
- Need to expand eval set to include 100 samples focused on code and table-writing prompts (these are where q4 drops most).
- For llm-serving default routing: add a prompt classifier that detects tables/code and routes to higher-precision variants. Prototype classifier using a small finetuned classifier (train on 2k examples).

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO Alex: run full batch throughput sweep for gptj-q4 on A10x GPUs for bs=1,4,8,16 and record tokens/sec. (target by 2026-03-19)
- TODO Maya: prepare the 100-code/table prompts (can reuse prompts/code sections from GH issue 452).
- TODO Jordan: add a small eval to look for tokenization mismatch around triple-backticks and fenced code. Maybe it's tokenizer config mismatch between bnb and our pretokenizer.
- Check if bitsandbytes q4 uses the same tokenizer config we're shipping in Redwood. If not, align or spool a postprocess step removing bad special tokens.

Notes on quant config details:
- bnb q4_0 vs q4_k: q4_k seems to preserve performance better on some weights but increases memory; try q4_k on gptj for a narrower test.
- llama.cpp q4_0 was done on CPU VM with AVX512 disabled; repeat on a VM with AVX2/AVX512 to see speedup (maybe p50 improves to ~80ms/token).

Experiment log (short):
- 2026-03-17 10:30 - spun up 2x A10x in dev pool, loaded gptj-6b.f16 and gptj-6b.q4 (bnb)
- 2026-03-17 11:05 - first 50-sample run showed q4 repetition; flagged for human review
- 2026-03-17 12:20 - ran 200-sample full run, saved outputs to out/ folder, started heuristic scoring job
- 2026-03-18 09:00 - human spot-check completed on 20 samples (Maya + Alex)

Quick heuristics / checkpoints we should track in CI for future runs:
- tokenization consistency check (hash of tokenizer config + vocab size) -> fail if mismatch across build artifacts
- mean length-of-response distribution shift > 15% triggers regression alert (q4 might truncate more)
- repetition rate (5-gram repetition > threshold) -> flag model variant

Notes to self (reminder):
- Keep sample set stable across runs; store seed and prompt list in GH; create a small README in eval/prompts explaining selection.
- Check GH PR #678 for updated model config; it mentions a tokenizer fix that might address the backtick issue.

Loose thoughts/brainstorm:
- Could integrate cheap classifier at the front of the Router that tags requests as CODE/TABLE/STREAMING and automatically weights routing to f16 variants for those. This would be a high-impact low-effort addition for Redwood Optimize.
- For Dedicated suggestions, present customers with estimated cost delta if they select q4 variant (tokens/sec improvement and $/1M tokens saved). Need clear UX messaging around "expected quality drop" with an example.

End of scratchpad for 2026-03-18. Will add numeric CSV outputs next to this doc after batch-throughput runs complete.
summary: Scratchpad capturing quick eval runs and quantization notes for gptj-6b and redwood variants. Contains commands, preliminary metrics, human spot-check results, TO-DOs, and action items for routing and CI checks.
